title: Regional allocation broker: deterministic leases and adaptive overflow policies
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We currently route tenant requests primarily by dedicated affinity and fall back to hosted endpoints when dedicated capacity is exhausted. Recent incidents show noisy tenants rapidly draining soft-reserves and producing cascaded overspill across regions. Goals: design a deterministic regional allocation broker that issues short-lived deterministic leases for dedicated lanes, enforces adaptive overflow throttles for hosted spillback, and provides variant demotion rules to preserve latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Broker can grant deterministic leases per-tenant with TTL and renewal semantics; 2) Overflow path triggers adaptive throttles when per-tenant spill rate exceeds configured thresholds; 3) Model variant demotion for overflow uses configured policy table and is reversible; 4) Rollout includes canary with automated rollback on >3% p50 latency regression or token error-rate increase >0.5% within 30m; 5) End-to-end test harness and dashboard showing per-tenant lease churn, spill rate, and latency percentiles.
scope: Implement broker control-plane and lightweight runtime hooks: lease allocator, priority decay, spill throttle controller, variant-demote policy engine. Integrate with existing placement service and billing meter. Provide admin UI controls in Console for per-tenant overrides and emergency evacuation.
out_of_scope: Full redesign of autoscaler, persistent workload reshuffling across regions, long-term pricing changes. KMS/HSM integration for private deployments is out of scope for this ticket.
constraints_and_risks:
- Deterministic leases add marginal control-plane state and complexity for recovering from partitioned controllers.
- Aggressive demotion may cause quality regressions; need safe beta flags.
- Overly strict throttles could violate enterprise SLAs; must expose per-tenant grace windows and soft-reserve tokens.
implementation_notes:
- Lease semantics: grantLease(tenant, region, ttl, graceTokens). TTL default 30s, renewal window 10s.
- Spill controller: proportional-integral controller with backoff factor based on recent spill rate and global capacity headroom.
- Variant demotion table lives in config-service with staged rollout via feature-flag.
- Fallback strategy: prefer same-region hosted variants first, then geo-nearest tiered fallback, respecting data residency tags.
- Metrics to emit: lease_grants, lease_renewals, lease_evictions, spill_count, spill_rate, demote_actions, demote_reverts, p50/p95_latency_by_path.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease allocator and spill controller; integration tests simulating noisy tenants and capacity drain; chaos test that kills controller and verifies leases expire cleanly and system recovers; canary in us-west with two tenants and synthetic traffic ramp to validate rollback triggers.
monitoring_and_rollout: Phase 1: feature-flagged canary in us-west (5% traffic) with monitoring alarms: p50 latency change >3%, error-rate +0.5%, spill_rate > threshold. Phase 2: gradual ramp to 25% then global if stable for 72h. Provide dashboard panels and alerts to oncall. Include a manual kill-switch in Console.
migration_and_billing: New telemetry needed to account for leased dedicated lanes vs hosted spillbacks for accurate billing. Work with billing team to tag tokens consumed under lease vs overflow. Migration will be backward compatible; default to existing behavior when broker disabled.
security_and_compliance: No new data plane changes. Control-plane state includes tenant IDs and region assignments; ensure access control for Console overrides is gated by RBAC. Audit logs must record lease grants/evictions for compliance reviews.
open_decisions:
1) TTL length trade-off: 30s (lower churn) vs 10s (faster recovery) — currently proposing 30s.
2) PI controller coefficients for spill backoff — tuning required in canary.
3) Whether to permit cross-region demotion for data-residency-constrained tenants — default: deny unless explicit opt-in.
